title: Tensor-Hom comparison and precomposition under a natural tensor functor
statement: Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be small sites in a common universe, $R$ and $S$ sheaves of commutative rings on them, and $U:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ a functor. Use the tensor and evaluation notation of [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data], with the ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Suppose $t_{M,Q}:U(M\otimes Q)\simeq UM\otimes UQ$ are isomorphisms satisfying $U(1_M\otimes f)t_{M,H}=t_{M,Q}(1_{UM}\otimes U(f))$ for every $f:Q\to H$. For $M,N$, write $H=\mathcal Hom_S(M,N)$ and $b=\operatorname{curry}(t_{M,H}^{-1}U(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}))$. Then for every $f:Q\to H$, one has $U(\operatorname{uncurry}(f))=t_{M,Q}(1_{UM}\otimes (U(f)b))\mathrm{ev}_{UM,UN}$, in diagrammatic composition order. No faithfulness or preservation of internal Hom by U is assumed.

source.place: lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor and its naturality in the tensor factor; explicit functorial transpose calculation written by D4.

proof.text: Express uncurrying f as (1 tensor f) followed by evaluation, using the tensor-Hom adjunction. Apply U and its composition law. Naturality of t moves U(1 tensor f) to the right of t and introduces t inverse at the Hom object. By the inverse laws of the adjunction, t inverse followed by U evaluation is the untranspose of b. Tensor functoriality combines U(f) and b, yielding the displayed identity. Every step is a functoriality or adjunction identity, and no nonemptiness or nonzero assumption is needed.

theorem tensorHomComparison_precomp
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u}}
    (U : Modules S ⥤ Modules R)
    (t : ∀ M N : Modules S, U.obj (tensorObj M N) ≅ tensorObj (U.obj M) (U.obj N))
    (ht : ∀ (M Q H : Modules S) (f : Q ⟶ H),
      U.map (tensorMap (𝟙 M) f) ≫ (t M H).hom =
        (t M Q).hom ≫ tensorMap (𝟙 (U.obj M)) (U.map f))
    (M N Q : Modules S) (f : Q ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := S) M N) :
    U.map ((SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv (R := S) M Q N).symm f) =
      (t M Q).hom ≫ tensorMap (𝟙 (U.obj M))
        (U.map f ≫ SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv (R := R) _ _ _
          ((t M (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := S) M N)).inv ≫
            U.map (evaluationMap M N))) ≫ evaluationMap (U.obj M) (U.obj N)
